dek: Two Kings Canyon waterfalls, Mist Falls and Roaring River Falls, with fees and safety notes. One $35 pass also covers Sequoia National Park.
overview: Kings Canyon National Park shares an entrance pass with Sequoia National Park. We cover two waterfalls inside Kings Canyon: Mist Falls and Roaring River Falls.

Visitors review the two about equally, and neither has a published distance, elevation or difficulty in our files. They are about 4.6 miles apart in a straight line, so they are separate outings rather than one hike.
fallsIntro: Both waterfalls are inside the park boundary. We don't have trail details for either, so check distances and conditions with the park.
plan: The same $35 pass covers Kings Canyon, Sequoia and the Hume Lake District of Sequoia National Forest for up to seven days, and no reservation is needed to enter. That means a Kings Canyon day and a Sequoia day can share one entrance receipt. We don't have trail or road times for either waterfall, so confirm access with the park.
flow: The nearest gauge with a complete record is the Marble Fork of the Kaweah River near Lodgepole (USGS 11206820), about 12.5 miles from Roaring River Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in June at about 100 cubic feet per second and was lowest in October at about 1.
It is a different river system from Mist Falls, so treat it as a regional snowmelt calendar rather than a flow report for either waterfall.
feesLead: One vehicle pass covers Kings Canyon, Sequoia and the Hume Lake District. Visitors who are not US residents pay an added $100 per person.
access: No reservation is needed to enter, but campgrounds are reservation-only and the park says summer sites are extremely limited. The weather page says Cedar Grove is usually open to vehicles from late spring into early fall, and roads can close after winter storms until they are plowed. Mist Falls is filed under Big Pine and Roaring River Falls under Three Rivers. Those are the nearest towns in our index, not trailheads.
safety: The park says every river in Sequoia and Kings Canyon is extremely hazardous in spring and early summer because snowmelt makes the water cold and fast. That applies to any waterfall visit here. We have no trail-specific warnings on file for Mist Falls or Roaring River Falls.
